question: Can classical kernel ridge regression be made adaptive to sparse coordinates and hierarchical polynomial structure by repeatedly estimating derivative-based feature importance and reweighting the input kernel?

key_findings.claim: A kernel predictor's derivatives can identify influential coordinates even when the predictor itself has nonvanishing generalization error.
key_findings.evidence: For polynomial-scaling samples n=d^(p+delta), the empirical squared coordinate derivative estimates the population weight of the degree-p truncation plus controlled higher-degree and noise terms; this separates feature detection from full prediction.

key_findings.claim: A derivative-norm estimator recovers a square-root factor in dimension for detecting the next polynomial degree, motivating a mixture of two importance signals.
key_findings.evidence: The DN estimator differentiates the kernel predictor's RKHS norm with respect to coordinate weights. Averaging it with empirical squared input gradients changes the relevant coefficient from d^(2delta-2) to d^(delta-1), allowing sub-square-root sample regimes in the motivating example.

key_findings.claim: Iteratively Reweighted Kernel Machines learn sparse hierarchical polynomials whose leap complexity is finite under strong asymptotic assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: Each iteration fits KRR on freshly sampled, coordinate-reweighted data and updates normalized weights from empirical gradients and DN scores. Theorem 4.9 gives consistency for the maximal (p+1)-leap component after O(1) rounds when sample size is d^(p+delta), sparsity grows slowly enough, and kernel/nondegeneracy conditions hold.

key_findings.claim: The theory is not distribution free despite the algorithm being generally applicable.
key_findings.evidence: The strongest results assume Gaussian or uniform-hypercube covariates, low-degree sparse polynomials, analytic inner-product kernels with nonnegative derivatives, fresh independent data each round, and asymptotics in ambient dimension.

key_findings.claim: Experiments extend beyond the theorem and show competitive tabular and epistasis performance, but the broad benchmark does not favor IRKM over its closest RFM baseline.
key_findings.evidence: Across 121 tabular tasks, IRKM averages 84.69% accuracy and Friedman rank 25.80 versus RFM's 85.15% and 20.37; both exceed the listed random forest and neural-network baselines. Synthetic sparse, rotated, and epistatic tasks often favor IRKM/RFM under the authors' sweeps.

method.core_idea: Turn prediction gradients into an explicit feature-learning loop for kernel machines.
method.mechanism: Fit KRR with a coordinate-weighted kernel, compute normalized empirical squared input gradients and a kernel derivative-norm score, mix them with a safeguard floor, resample and refit; a matrix-valued extension uses average gradient outer products for unknown rotated subspaces.
assumptions: Sparse polynomial target with bounded degree and finite leap complexity
Gaussian or uniform-hypercube covariates for theory
Fresh independent samples at each theoretical iteration
Influential-coordinate derivatives stay bounded away from zero

techniques.role: Uses squared input derivatives of a KRR predictor to rank coordinates.
Adds a DN score that exposes one higher polynomial degree at improved sample scaling.
Feeds learned coordinate importance back into the next kernel fit to uncover hierarchical interactions.
Generalizes diagonal weights to a matrix for multi-index functions in an unknown basis.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic Gaussian/hypercube sparse polynomials and rotated multi-index targets
evaluations.result: IRKM/RFM mixtures usually beat plain KRR and the authors' tuned fully connected networks
evaluations.baseline: plain kernels, alpha=0 reweighting, and Adam-trained MLPs

evaluations.result: IRKM 84.69%/25.80, close to but below RFM 85.15%/20.37
evaluations.baseline: RFM, random forest, and neural network

evaluations.result: plots report competitive feature-interaction detection across three heritabilities

limitations: The 130-page theory applies to stylized sparse polynomials and restrictive covariate/kernel conditions.
Fresh data per iteration is central to analysis but unavailable in most finite datasets; experiments reuse data on tabular tasks.
Each round solves an n-by-n kernel system, limiting large-n scalability.
The matrix-valued RFM extension is mainly empirical and the authors only conjecture transfer of the full theory.
failure_modes: Early false-negative weights can suppress later interactions despite the safeguard.
Correlated or heavy-tailed covariates can confound derivative scores.
High leap complexity restores polynomial-in-d sample cost.
Repeated reuse of a small dataset can overfit feature weights and invalidate fresh-sample reasoning.
reusable_insights: A poor predictor can still contain useful derivative-based feature information.
Mix complementary estimators when their signal and noise scale differently with dimension.
Use a positive safeguard so recursive feature elimination can recover from early mistakes.
open_questions: Can comparable finite-sample bounds hold without fresh resampling?
Can randomized solvers or inducing points preserve feature recovery at large n?
Does full-matrix reweighting provably learn unknown multi-index subspaces with similar complexity?

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanism of feature learning in deep fully connected networks and kernel machines that recursively learn features
competitive_landscape.difference: This work introduces AGOP-based Recursive Feature Machines empirically; IRKM adds a derivative-norm signal, coordinate-specialized theory, fresh-sample safeguards, and leap-complexity guarantees.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Recursive Feature Machines provably recover low-rank matrices
competitive_landscape.difference: Linear RFM establishes sparse linear and low-rank recovery and connects RFM to IRLS; the reviewed work treats nonlinear sparse functions and hierarchical polynomial interactions.

competitive_landscape.title: The merged-staircase property: a necessary and nearly sufficient condition for SGD learning of sparse functions on two-layer neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Merged-staircase characterizes when nonlinear two-layer SGD learns sparse Boolean functions and proves linear-feature methods insufficient; IRKM changes the kernel itself across fits, escaping the fixed-feature lower bound for finite-leap functions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Iterative derivative-based reweighting gives classical kernels both sparse feature learning and hierarchical learning at neural-network-like sample complexity.
novelty_assessment.evidence: New DN-estimator asymptotics and maximal-leap recovery theorems complement broad synthetic and tabular experiments.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the DN-plus-gradient estimator and leap-complexity analysis. It extends rather than displaces RFM/IRLS, and its practical generality is less established than its stylized theory.

reviewer_notes: Reviewed the full 130-page extraction, including assumptions, theorem statements, proof roadmap, all main experiments, and conclusion. Primary competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
